title: Isaac and the ram
text: God asked Abraham to show how much he trusted Him. Abraham loved his son Isaac very much, but he trusted God even more. Abraham and Isaac climbed a mountain together carrying wood. Isaac asked where the lamb was, and Abraham answered that God would provide one. Just when Abraham was ready to obey, an angel of the Lord called out and told him to stop. Isaac was safe! Abraham then saw a ram caught in a bush, and God had provided exactly what was needed. The Church also sees this story as a picture of Jesus, God's own Son, who later gave Himself for us. The lesson for us is that God can be trusted, and He always takes care of those who trust Him.

verse.text: My son, God will provide himself a lamb for a burnt offering

title: Jacob's ladder
text: Jacob was traveling alone, far from home, and he was probably feeling worried. When night came he lay down with a stone for a pillow. In a dream he saw a ladder reaching from earth up to heaven, and angels of God going up and down on it. God spoke to Jacob and promised to be with him and keep him wherever he went. When Jacob woke up he said that God was in this place, and he had not known it. He named the place Bethel, which means house of God. We may feel alone sometimes, but God is with us wherever we go, even when we cannot see Him.

verse.text: Behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places whither thou goest

title: Joshua and the walls of Jericho
text: After Moses, God chose Joshua to lead His people into the land He promised them. The city of Jericho had tall, strong walls, and nobody could get in. God gave Joshua a surprising plan. The people did not fight. They walked quietly around the city once a day for six days, with priests carrying the ark and blowing trumpets. On the seventh day they walked around seven times, then the people shouted, and the walls fell down. Joshua obeyed God even when the plan seemed strange. God had told him to be strong and not to be afraid, because He would be with him. When we obey God and trust Him, nothing is too big for Him.

verse.text: Be strong and of a good courage; be not afraid, neither be thou dismayed: for the LORD thy God is with thee whithersoever thou goest.

title: Ruth stays with Naomi
text: Ruth was a young woman whose husband had died. Her mother-in-law Naomi decided to go back to her homeland of Bethlehem, and told Ruth to stay with her own family. But Ruth loved Naomi and said she would go wherever Naomi went, and that Naomi's God would be her God. In Bethlehem, Ruth worked hard gathering leftover grain in the field of a kind man named Boaz. Boaz noticed her goodness and took care of her. Later they married. Ruth became the great-grandmother of King David, and she is named in the family line of Jesus. Her story shows how loyalty, hard work and kindness are rewarded by God.

verse.text: thy people shall be my people, and thy God my God

title: God calls young Samuel
text: Samuel was a boy who helped the old priest Eli in the house of the Lord. One night Samuel heard a voice call his name. He ran to Eli and said, Here I am, but Eli had not called him. This happened three times. Then Eli understood that it was God calling. Eli told Samuel that if he heard the voice again, he should say, Speak, Lord, for your servant is listening. Samuel did, and God spoke to him. Samuel grew up to be a faithful prophet and helped lead God's people. God can speak to children too, and we can listen to Him by praying, reading the Bible and obeying what is good.

verse.text: Speak; for thy servant heareth.

title: Elijah and the ravens
text: Elijah was a prophet who loved God and spoke the truth to a king who did not follow God. There was no rain for a long time, and food became hard to find. God told Elijah to hide by a brook, and God sent ravens to bring him bread and meat each morning and evening. Later God sent him to a poor widow who had only a little flour and oil, and God made her jar and her oil last until the rain came again. God took care of Elijah in surprising ways. Later on Mount Carmel, Elijah prayed and God answered with fire from heaven. The story reminds us that God knows what we need and cares for us.

title: Gideon and the three hundred
text: God's people were being troubled by enemies, and God chose Gideon to help them. Gideon felt small and unsure, but God said He would be with him. Gideon gathered many soldiers, but God said there were too many, so people would think they had won by their own strength. In the end only three hundred men were left. Gideon gave each man a trumpet and a clay jar with a torch hidden inside. At night they blew the trumpets, broke the jars and shouted, and the enemy ran away confused. The victory belonged to God. We do not need to be big or strong, because God can do great things through people who trust Him.

title: Job trusts God
text: Job was a good man who loved God. He had a big family and many animals, and life was happy. Then very hard things happened. He lost his animals, his children and his health. Job was very sad and he did not understand why, and some friends did not comfort him well. But Job never stopped trusting God. He said the name of the Lord should be blessed. In the end God spoke to Job, and God gave him healing and blessed him again with a new family and more than before. Job's story teaches us that when life is sad or confusing, we can still trust that God is near and loves us.

verse.text: the LORD gave, and the LORD hath taken away; blessed be the name of the LORD.

title: Solomon asks for wisdom
text: When Solomon became king after his father David, he was young. One night God said to him in a dream, Ask what I should give you. Solomon could have asked for riches, a long life or power. Instead he asked for an understanding heart so that he could rule God's people well and know right from wrong. God was pleased that he asked for this. God gave him great wisdom, and also gave him the riches and honor he had not asked for. Solomon later built the temple in Jerusalem for God. The story teaches us to ask God first for wisdom and goodness, and to trust Him with the rest.

verse.text: Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.

title: The parable of the sower
text: Jesus told this story to teach how we receive God's word. A farmer went out to scatter seed. Some seed fell on the path, and birds ate it. Some fell on rocky ground with thin soil, and it grew fast but dried up. Some fell among thorns, which choked it. But some fell on good soil and grew into a great harvest. Jesus explained that the seed is God's word. The hearts that are like good soil listen, understand and keep the word, and then they bear fruit by doing good. We can make our hearts good soil by listening in church, reading the Bible, praying and doing what Jesus teaches.

verse.text: Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.

title: The lost coin
text: Jesus told a story about a woman who had ten silver coins and lost one. She did not say it did not matter. She lit a lamp, swept the whole house and searched carefully until she found it. When she found it, she called her friends and neighbors and said to rejoice with her. Jesus said that in the same way there is joy among the angels of God when one person turns back to Him. Every one of us is precious to God, and He does not give up on anyone. If we ever feel lost or have done wrong, God is happy when we come back to Him.

verse.text: Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.

title: Jesus heals blind Bartimaeus
text: Bartimaeus was a blind man who sat by the road near Jericho and asked people for help. When he heard that Jesus was passing by, he called out loudly, Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me! Some people told him to be quiet, but he cried out even more. Jesus stopped and asked for him to be brought. Jesus asked what he wanted, and Bartimaeus said he wanted to see. Jesus told him his faith had made him well, and right away he could see. Then Bartimaeus followed Jesus on the road. His story shows that Jesus hears us when we call, and He cares for everyone, even when others ignore them.

verse.text: Jesus, thou son of David, have mercy on me.

title: Jesus raises Lazarus
text: Lazarus lived in Bethany with his sisters Mary and Martha, and Jesus loved them. When Lazarus became sick and died, his sisters were very sad. By the time Jesus arrived, Lazarus had been in the tomb four days. Jesus saw how sad everyone was, and the Bible says Jesus wept. Jesus told Martha that He is the resurrection and the life. Then He went to the tomb, asked for the stone to be taken away, prayed to the Father, and called with a loud voice, Lazarus, come forth! Lazarus came out alive. This miracle shows that Jesus has power over death and that He cares deeply when we are sad.

verse.text: I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live:

title: Zacchaeus climbs the tree
text: Zacchaeus was a short man who collected taxes in Jericho, and many people did not like him because he had been unfair with money. When he heard Jesus was coming, he wanted to see Him, but the crowd was too tall. So he ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree. Jesus stopped under the tree, looked up and called him by name. He said He would stay at Zacchaeus's house that day. Zacchaeus was so happy. He promised to give half of what he had to the poor, and to give back four times what he had taken unfairly. Jesus loves us and welcomes us, and when we meet Him our hearts change.

verse.text: For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.

title: Why does the priest wear special clothes?
text: During the Holy Liturgy the priest and the deacons wear special clothes called vestments. They are not for fashion. They are set apart for serving at the altar, just like a special uniform for a special job. The vestments are often white, which is a sign of purity. Our Coptic teaching says the white tunic reminds us of the angels who serve God. The deacon also wears a stole across his shoulder, and it reminds us that a deacon serves like an angel. The colors and crosses on the vestments are beautiful because we are offering our best to God. When we see them, we remember that the Liturgy is heavenly worship and we are joining in with the angels.

title: What is a monastery?
text: A monastery is a place where monks live. Monks are men who give their lives to God, pray many hours a day, work with their hands and live simply, often far from busy cities. Women who do this are called nuns and live in convents. The first monks in the world lived in Egypt, and St. Antony is called the father of monks. Later St. Pachomius started monks living together as a community. Monasteries in Egypt are still alive today, such as in the desert of Wadi El Natrun. Many popes of our church were monks before they became popes. Monks pray for the whole world, and many families visit monasteries to pray and be blessed.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we go to church on Sunday?
text: Sunday is the day Jesus rose from the dead. That makes it the Lord's Day, a little Pascha every week, when we remember that Jesus is alive and has defeated death. The Church has gathered for worship on the first day of the week since the early days of the Apostles. On Sunday we pray together, hear the Gospel and receive Holy Communion in the Holy Liturgy. It is not just a rule. It is a happy family meeting where we meet Jesus, see our church friends and thank God for the whole week. Going every Sunday helps us grow closer to God, just as eating regularly helps our bodies grow.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: This is the day which the LORD hath made; we will rejoice and be glad in it.

title: Why do we kiss the icons and the cross?
text: When we enter a church, many of us kiss the icons or the cross, or bow in front of them. We are not praying to wood or paint. Think of how you might kiss a photo of someone you love, like your grandmother. The kiss shows love and respect for the person in the picture, such as Jesus, St. Mary or a saint. The honor passes on to the one the icon shows. We also kiss the priest's hand cross when he blesses us. This is the way our church shows reverence and love. We worship God alone, and we honor the saints because they belong to Him and pray for us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we ask the priest for a blessing?
text: After the Liturgy or when we meet Abouna, we often ask him for a blessing. The priest holds a cross, and we kiss it and his hand. The priest is not the source of the blessing. God is. Abouna is the servant of God who prays for us in the name of the Lord, and the hand cross reminds us of Jesus. It also shows respect and thankfulness for his work and his prayers for us. Children can do this too. It is a polite and holy greeting, and it helps us remember that God is always the one who blesses and protects us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: The Jesus Prayer
text: The Jesus Prayer is a very short prayer that we can say anywhere, quietly in our hearts. The usual words are, Lord Jesus Christ, Son of God, have mercy on me, a sinner. It is based on what the blind man Bartimaeus cried out to Jesus and on the prayer of the tax collector in Jesus's story. We can say it when we wake up, when we are walking, when we are scared, or when we cannot fall asleep. Saying it slowly helps us remember that Jesus is near and ready to help us. Some Orthodox Christians use a prayer rope to count them, but you do not need one. It is a good habit to start when you are young.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why do we pray towards the east?
text: In the Coptic Orthodox Church the altar is placed at the east end of the church, and the priest and people face east when they pray. Early Christians prayed this way. The east is where the sun rises, and it reminds us of Jesus, whom the Bible calls the Sun of righteousness, and of the light He brings to the world. It also reminds us of Eden, the garden God planted in the east, and our hope of returning to heaven. We also look forward to the second coming of Jesus. It is a special way to help us remember who we are praying to. At home you can pray facing east too, but God hears you in any direction.

verse.text: But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings;

title: Why do some people take their shoes off in church?
text: When God spoke to Moses at the burning bush, He told him to take his shoes off, because the ground was holy. In the same way, some Coptic churches have the custom of taking shoes off, or being very careful, in holy places, especially near the altar area, which is called the Haykal. It is a way to show respect and awe, because God is truly present there. Custom can be different from one church to another, so follow what your church and Abouna ask. Even when shoes stay on, we show respect by walking quietly, bowing and crossing ourselves. What matters most is a respectful heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: put off thy shoes from off thy feet, for the place whereon thou standest is holy ground.

title: What are the Gospel and the Bible reading in church?
text: During the Holy Liturgy we listen to readings from the Bible. There are readings from the letters of the Apostles, from the Acts of the Apostles, from the Psalms and then the Gospel, which tells about the life and words of Jesus. When the Gospel is read, the deacons and the people stand, because we are listening to Jesus Himself speaking. The priest reads the Gospel and then often someone explains it in a sermon. The readings are chosen by the Church for each day, so we hear the whole Bible over time. Listening carefully and thinking about what we hear helps us live as God wants during the week.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Why should we share?
text: Sharing means letting others use or have some of what we have, like a toy, a snack or our time. It can feel hard, but Jesus shared too. He shared five loaves and two fish with a huge crowd, and everyone had enough. When we share, we show love and make other people happy, and we remember that everything we have is a gift from God. The Bible says it is more blessed to give than to receive. You can share with your friends, your family, and with those in need through the church. Even a small share, like half your sandwich, makes a big difference.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: It is more blessed to give than to receive.

title: Why do we obey our parents?
text: God gave us parents to love us, teach us and keep us safe. The Bible tells children to obey their parents in the Lord, and the Ten Commandments tell us to honor our father and mother. When we obey, we show love and respect, and we learn to listen to God too. Even Jesus, when He was a boy, obeyed St. Mary and St. Joseph. Obeying does not mean we are never allowed to ask questions or share how we feel. We can speak politely. Sometimes it is hard, and we make mistakes. When we do, we can say sorry and try again. God is pleased when we obey with a happy heart.

verse.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord: for this is right.

title: How can I be brave?
text: Being brave does not mean you never feel afraid. It means doing the right thing even when you feel afraid. David was brave when he faced Goliath, Daniel was brave in the lions' den, and the martyrs were brave because they loved Jesus. Their courage came from trusting God, who was with them. When you feel scared at school, in the dark or at the doctor, you can pray, make the sign of the cross and say a short prayer like the Jesus Prayer. You can also tell a parent or a teacher how you feel. God promises to be with us, and that makes us strong.

verse.text: What time I am afraid, I will trust in thee.

title: Why does God let bad things happen?
text: This is a big question, and even grown ups wonder about it. God made the world good, and He gave people freedom to choose. Sometimes people choose wrong things, and the world has sickness and sadness because of sin. God does not cause evil. He is good, and He loves us. When bad things happen He is close to us and sad with us. Jesus wept when His friend died. God also comforts us through other people who help us, and He can bring good even out of hard times. We may not always understand why, but we can pray, tell a parent or Abouna how we feel, and trust that God never leaves us.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

title: Where is heaven?
text: Heaven is where God lives, and where the angels and the saints are with Him. It is a place of joy and light, with no sadness, sickness or fear. The Bible says Jesus went to prepare a place for us in His Father's house. We do not know exactly where heaven is or what it looks like, because it is bigger than anything we can imagine. We know that heaven is not far away from God's love, because God is with us now too. Everyone who loves Jesus and follows Him hopes to live with Him forever. We prepare for heaven by loving God, loving others and asking forgiveness when we do wrong.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: In my Father's house are many mansions

title: Do angels watch over me?
text: Yes. The Bible says God sends His angels to take care of those who love Him. Our church teaches that each person has a guardian angel who looks after us, protects us and prays for us. Angels are God's messengers. We cannot see them, but they are near us, especially when we pray and when we are in church during the Liturgy. We can ask for the help of Archangel Michael, Archangel Gabriel and Archangel Raphael. We do not worship angels. We worship God alone. Angels help us because God asks them to. You can thank God for your guardian angel in your evening prayer.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For he shall give his angels charge over thee, to keep thee in all thy ways.

title: Why do we pray?
text: Praying is talking with God. He is our loving Father, and like any child who loves their family, we want to talk to Him. We can thank Him, say sorry, ask for help, and pray for other people. God already knows everything, but He loves to hear from us, and prayer draws us closer to Him. It also changes us. We become more kind, more peaceful and more thankful. We can pray anywhere and anytime, in our own words or with the prayers of the Church, like the Lord's Prayer and the Agpeya. We should pray in the morning, before meals, and before sleeping. Jesus Himself prayed often.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: in every thing by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving let your requests be made known unto God.

title: Why should we read the Bible?
text: The Bible is God's word to us. It tells us who God is, how He made the world and how much He loves us. It tells the story of Jesus and teaches us how to live. When we read it, we get to know God better, just like getting to know a friend by listening to him. The Bible gives us comfort when we are sad, courage when we are afraid and wisdom when we need to choose. You can read a little each day, like a story from a children's Bible or a Gospel chapter, and ask Abouna or a servant when you do not understand something. It is like a lamp that lights our way.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Thy word is a lamp unto my feet, and a light unto my path.

title: What is sin?
text: Sin is when we do something that goes against God's love, like lying, hurting someone, being greedy or disobeying on purpose. It can also be not doing the good we should do. Sin hurts us, other people and our friendship with God. Everyone makes mistakes and does wrong sometimes, even grown ups. But God does not stop loving us. That is why Jesus came, to save us and forgive us. When we sin, we can say sorry to God, say sorry to the person we hurt, and try to do better. In the sacrament of Confession the priest prays for us in God's name and we receive forgiveness.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: For all have sinned, and come short of the glory of God;

title: What is repentance?
text: Repentance means turning back to God. In Greek the word is metanoia, which means a change of mind and heart. When we do something wrong, we feel sorry, we say so to God, we decide to stop and we try to fix what we can. Then we do better. The story of the prodigal son shows repentance. He went back to his father, and his father ran to welcome him. God is like that father. He is always happy when we come back. We repent in our daily prayers and in the sacrament of Confession. Repenting is not only for big sins. It is a normal part of every Christian's life.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: there is joy in the presence of the angels of God over one sinner that repenteth.

title: Being patient
text: Patience means waiting calmly without getting upset. It is hard to wait for a turn, for dinner, for a birthday or for someone to finish talking. The Bible shows people who waited for God, like Abraham, who waited for his son, and Noah, who waited for the flood to end. When we are patient, we show love, because we give other people time. We can practice patience by taking a slow breath, saying a short prayer and thinking of others. God is patient with us too. He waits for us to learn and grow, and does not give up on us. Ask Him to help you.

verse.text: Wait on the LORD: be of good courage, and he shall strengthen thine heart: wait, I say, on the LORD.

title: What is humility?
text: Humility means not thinking we are better than other people and remembering that all good things come from God. A humble person does not brag, and is happy to help, listen and say sorry. Jesus is our best example. He is God, yet He washed the feet of His disciples to show us how to serve. Humble people are not weak. They are strong because they know God is their helper. Saints like St. Antony and St. Moses the Black grew in humility, and God honored them. You can practice humility by thanking others, letting a friend go first and not boasting about winning.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he shall lift you up.

title: Does God hear me when I pray?
text: Yes, God always hears you. He hears every prayer, even a whisper or a prayer without words, and even if you pray in your heart at school. Jesus told us that God our Father knows what we need before we ask, and still He wants us to ask. Sometimes God answers right away, sometimes He asks us to wait, and sometimes the answer is different from what we hoped, because He sees what is best. When it seems He is not answering, we keep praying and trust that He loves us. We can also ask Abouna or a servant for help. You are never too small or too young for God to listen to you.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: The righteous cry, and the LORD heareth, and delivereth them out of all their troubles.

title: Is God everywhere? Can He see me?
text: Yes. God is everywhere at the same time, and He loves us so much that He is always near. The Bible says nowhere can we go to be away from His presence. That means we are never alone, whether we are at home, at school, in the dark or in a hospital. God sees us, and not to catch us doing something wrong, but because He cares like a loving father. He sees our good deeds and our sadness too. Knowing He is close helps us make good choices and gives us comfort. We can talk to Him at any moment, with a short prayer in our heart.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?

title: What if someone is mean to me?
text: It hurts when someone is unkind or teases us. First, remember that you are precious and loved by God. It is okay to tell a trusted grown up, like a parent, a teacher or Abouna, and it is okay to walk away. We should not hit back or say mean words. Jesus taught us to treat others the way we want to be treated, and to pray for those who are unkind. Praying for them does not mean what they did was okay. It means we ask God to help them change. If you see someone else being treated badly, be kind to that person and get help. Kindness is strong.

verse.text: Therefore all things whatsoever ye would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them

title: What happens when someone we love dies?
text: When someone we love dies, we feel very sad, and that is okay. Crying shows how much we loved them. As Christians we believe that Jesus defeated death when He rose from the dead, so death is not the end. The souls of those who loved God are in His care, and one day we will all be raised. In church we pray for those who have passed away, and we remember them with love. The Bible says God will wipe away every tear. If you are sad, talk to your parents or Abouna, pray, and remember the good times. God is close to those who are sad.
source: Heavenly Visions kid summary of Coptic Orthodox teaching

verse.text: And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes;
